title: Re-baseline the work-readiness execution budget from 120 to 320 minutes

outcomes.statement: The tenant gate and the substrate gate enforce the same execution budget, and that budget is calibrated against the story-point scale the design phase actually uses rather than a figure derived from one incident.
outcomes.demo: `pnpm readiness:check` accepts a 320-minute single-outcome estimate and refuses 321 with WR_ESTIMATE_OVER_BUDGET; a grep for a budget-related 120 across the gate's scripts, schema and docs returns nothing.

uncertainties.statement: Whether the substrate already enforces 320, so the two gates genuinely disagree today.
uncertainties.resolution: It does. fcostudios__smp's project_configs carries execution_budget {enabled: true, max_readiness_minutes: 320, minutes_per_story_point: 104, calibration.min_samples: 2}, and the [Execution Budget Sizing] drift section names exactly US-019 and US-034 — the two 5SP stories — as over budget. The tenant gate still refuses anything above 120.

uncertainties.statement: Whether the scope table's line references are still accurate after CHG-034's four cuts landed.
uncertainties.resolution: The SITES are all correct; the LINE NUMBERS drifted, as expected. Re-located 2026-09-05: model.mjs:277 (was 305), schema:337 and :709 (were 340/712, shifted by the dead $defs.checkpoint removal), WORK_READINESS.md:31/56/335 (368 became 335 when the clock section was replaced), CLAUDE.md:67, test-work-readiness.mjs:225/398.

uncertainties.statement: Whether 320 is defensible given the calibration pairs are estimates, not actuals.
uncertainties.resolution: It is provisional and the CHG says so. docs/readiness/README.md records estimates running 2-3x under actuals. The rate is persisted in config, so revisiting it is a one-line diff once actuals.total exists on two items — that follow-through is named in the CHG, not deferred silently.
